assumptions_checked: planning_sd is a reasonable estimate of the true process spread (pilot data, history, or a stated guess)
provenance.method: n = (z*s/E)^2, rounded up (NIST/SEMATECH §7.2.1 CI-for-a-mean, solved for n)

value.plain_english: To estimate the average within +/-1.25 (your data's units) at 95% confidence -- using a planning estimate of spread (SD) of 6.5 -- collect at least 104 data points.

rule_of_thumb.rationale: Convention, not a derived law: 25-30 individual readings, in true time order, is the commonly-taught rule of thumb for a usable I-MR baseline -- a little above the 20-point floor this suite's own baseline tool (T-13) requires before it will freeze control limits, leaving room for a few points to be legitimately excluded as special causes. Collecting fewer is an honest, named shortfall -- not a hard stop the way T-13's own floor is.
